• Panels now reach the decorated frame on the left and right, as they already did at the top and bottom. The side columns keep their width and GAME OUTPUT, TANK and TARGET take the extra space.
  • GAME OUTPUT has a scrollbar. Scrolling up opens Mudlet's split view, with new text still arriving below.
  • Commands you type now appear in GAME OUTPUT, in Mudlet's command color and following the profile's command-echo setting. Text that scripts or Mudlet itself write to the main window is shown there too. Previously it went to the hidden main window.
  • Mudlet's log button records the game again. Previously server text was removed from the hidden main window as it was shown in GAME OUTPUT, so logs held only your commands. ui off now also shows the full session.
  • Long commands and messages wrap at the GAME OUTPUT width instead of breaking at Mudlet's wrap column, and links in them stay clickable. Script messages appear even when no game text follows them.
  • New ui set timestamps on shows the time each GAME OUTPUT line arrived, like the main window's clock button. Off by default.
  • GAME OUTPUT has its own search box next to the room name, replacing Mudlet's search box and F3, which only search the hidden main window. Press Enter or ▲ (Shift+F3) for the next older match and ▼ (F3) for the next newer one; the match is highlighted and scrolled into view. If Mudlet's F3 search option is on, it is paused while the UI is shown, and restored even if Mudlet was closed while the UI was showing.
  • New ui find <text> lists the latest GAME OUTPUT lines containing the text. Click one to scroll back to it.

• CHARACTER > SPELLS now opens on INTERFACE, which shows your class's preparation list (memorize, pray, commune, ...). The old LIST subtab is renamed SPELLS and comes second.
  • The spell master list loads for casters whose list spans more than one server page. Previously the pager stopped the capture and the panel stayed empty.
  • Typing your preparation command, or an abbreviation such as mem, refreshes INTERFACE. If you page through a typed list yourself, the panel waits for you, however long you read each page.
  • Clicking INTERFACE while the client is still learning your preparation command runs it as soon as the command is known.
  • Spell panels highlight titles and circles and dim future circles; INTERFACE explains when a character has no preparation command.

• GROUP, the SHIP bridge and context menus keep the dark panel background on every desktop theme. Previously the system palette could show through as light grey, making the green GROUP header hard to read.

• Keep the other GEAR list visible while inventory or equipment updates, and switch between them without requesting a new snapshot.
  • Skip a single unreadable item instead of hiding the whole list.
  • Clicking GEAR again retries an item subscription the server never answered.
  • Turning the damage tracker off and quickly back on no longer marks combat events as stopped by the server.

• Keep clickable server-provided web links and recipient colors in chat tabs and private conversation history.
  • Use the server clock and explicit session/body transitions, with text fallback on older servers.
  • Count outgoing applied damage, including secondary targets, once per scoped event and mark interrupted history incomplete.
  • Show paged owner inventory/equipment in GEAR, with safe snapshot-scoped item actions and requested direct-container contents.
  • Keep the HUD, room and map when the package starts or reloads while a character is already playing.
  • Show player chat text literally when the server sends no chat snapshot, and keep each message's own time when a private conversation is reopened.

• Show the latest ship information in SHIP as soon as another maximized panel is restored, instead of waiting for the next ship update.
  • Refit SHIP cards and buttons after transferring maximization between panels, even without new ship data.
  • Restore critical, damaged and sound text colors in the ship bridge.

• Keep game text moving during busy group updates: the GROUP panel now updates only what changed, once per burst of server updates, and waits until it is visible.
  • Keep your scroll position in GROUP when members' health or position changes.
  • Restore GROUP text colors for the weakest member, absent members, low movement and alert postures.

• Keep spell replies intact while other commands are in flight and require a primary click to start preparation.
  • Recover preparation estimates after rate-limited negotiation or reinstall, while retaining other add-ons’ subscriptions.
  • Preserve the original layout for rollback, remember the ROOM subtab, and keep CHAT clear of PLAYERS in short windows.
  • Preserve settings, custom commands and bid scores when saving fails.

• Combine MOBS and ITEMS in ROOM and give ROOM and PLAYERS the same default height.
  • Move inventory and equipment under GEAR. Open SPELLS for your spell list and the preparation command Duris reports for your character.
  • Show the server’s spell preparation estimate beside your position, with distinct paused and complete states.

• Render wilderness foregrounds and backgrounds with the profile's ANSI colors, preserving the server's white zone-marker backgrounds and terrain contrast instead of dimming them with a separate map palette.
  • Keep custom marker colors, grey city/road symbols and the player marker consistent with ordinary game text after movement, refresh and zoom.

• Mark your own health as YOU HP and identify the owner of tank and target bars explicitly, so a wounded pet or enemy cannot be mistaken for your character.
  • Correct the self-tank display when character identity arrives after the combat prompt, and keep health data with the correct combatant when tanks or assisted group members change.
  • Keep combat prompt fields separate when names contain prompt-like text or conditions contain a capital E; show unknown tank health when no current health data is available.
• Keep player, tank, target, and group HP bars within their panels when vamp healing exceeds maximum HP, while preserving actual HP values and percentages in their labels.

• Restore visible time output after the silent login query by recognizing the server's current reply format.
  • Stop suppressing time output after three seconds or another outgoing command, so missing or incomplete replies cannot hide later manual requests or time-display clicks.
  • Cancel the delayed login query when a manual time request or time-display click already supplies the HUD data.
  • Preserve character state and pending actions when ordinary text mentions the account menu; reset only at its actual bordered header.
  • Accept loot-split dice only from the local character with the requested sides and roll index, and use uniform weighted odds above 100 tickets.
  • Match Duris dawn/dusk announcements and query hours to the server clock.

• Replace the tall Duris banner with a slim bronze/obsidian perimeter and an original Stormwatch panorama, cropped without stretching.
  • Let panels use the recovered upper workspace in both presentation modes, with protected Panels/Reset clearance. Existing saved layouts remain compatible.
  • Keep ui set compactHeader on as the quiet gradient option; both settings retain the same frame and panel bounds. Missing or corrupt artwork falls back independently.

• Add the responsive Captain's Table Bridge with spatial armor/internal gauges, actual/ordered helm, arc badges, complete manifest, crew watch and contact bearing glass.
  • Retain selectable Details and a local Copy details action; persist the view preference and coalesce visible ship paints while hidden panels accept state.
  • SHIP refresh requests look ship; explicit Look ship, Look crew and Contacts actions send their named reference command once.
  • Clear entire ambiguous contact selections, preserve explicit weapon destruction state, and show both helm glyphs on a steady course.

• Show bridge weight/load, ordered navigation, display/raw stamina, explicit target, slot condition/timers/destruction, contact coordinates and both arc meanings when supplied by the server.
  • Associate ship snapshots by runtime vessel key, preserve safe legacy fallback, handle duplicate docked designations and keep server names literal.

Notable changes to the Duris Client Mudlet package. Versions follow Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH); see docs/RELEASING.md for what each part means here. Each version heading must match VERSION; the release workflow copies that section into the GitHub Release notes.

• Give private tell windows shared move, resize, minimize, maximize and recovery actions while retaining history and drafts.
  • Redraw stationary zone/wilderness maps from accepted data, including maximized maps with saved hidden/minimized state.
  • Preserve unread tells behind covered panels and acknowledge them, including the contact indicator, only on reveal.
  • Keep deferred map paints beneath covered output and clean up owned menus/callback references.
  • Carry portable layout replacement/rollback/recovery through the complete private-panel stack.

• Preserve unread tells behind a different maximized panel and acknowledge them only on reveal.
  • Redraw maximized maps using effective visibility, retaining saved hidden/minimized state.
  • Keep deferred map refreshes below covered output and carry forward compact-header/SHIP fixes.

• Give private tell windows the shared move, resize, minimize, maximize and recovery actions while retaining session history and drafts.
  • Redraw stationary zone and wilderness maps after panel/viewport changes without new network requests.
  • Clean up owned frame menus and old-Mudlet callback references on teardown.

• Organize SHIP into readable condition, weapon, crew, equipment, cargo and contact sections with labeled values, condition colors and separate ammunition, damage and timer status.
  • Preserve navigation, target controls, text fallback and empty-state clearing while handling older or partial ship payloads.
  • Restore the absolute SHIP scroll position after updates, including the adjustable dashboard viewport.

• Rebuild the dashboard as ten adjustable panels with title/border gestures, named home docking, locking, minimize, hide and maximize actions.
  • Add ui layout, ui panel, fixed Panels and Reset layout controls, and profile-local normalized layout persistence.
  • Keep game output visible and preserve scrollback and selected views during layout changes.
  • Keep event-driven map paints below a different maximized panel and reveal the latest accepted room on restore.
  • Replace existing saved layouts on Windows while retaining the previous file on failure.
  • Repaint stationary wilderness maps from accepted data after dashboard geometry changes.
  • Remove the inactive private-panel recovery placeholder; private frame controls arrive in the dependent integration PR.

• Rebuild the dashboard as ten adjustable panels with title/border gestures, named home docking, locking, minimize, hide and maximize actions.
  • Add ui layout, ui panel, fixed Panels and Reset layout controls, and profile-local normalized layout persistence.
  • Keep game output visible and preserve scrollback and selected views during layout changes.
  • Keep event-driven map paints below a different maximized panel and reveal the latest accepted room on restore.

• Add ui set compactHeader on|off, a saved option that collapses the illustrated header into a dark gradient and gives the recovered height to gameplay panels. Full artwork remains the default.
  • Recenter populated zone and wilderness maps when the header or window size changes, preserving map mode, cache and zoom.
  • Keep a paused mapper's display frozen during header changes, resize, and UI hide/show.
  • Preserve unread private tells received while the UI is hidden; opening the conversation reveals and marks them read.

• Add ui set compactHeader on|off, a saved option that collapses the illustrated header into a dark gradient and gives the recovered height to gameplay panels. Full artwork remains the default.
  • Recenter populated zone and wilderness maps when the header or window size changes, preserving map mode, cache and zoom.
  • Keep a paused mapper's display frozen during header changes, resize, and UI hide/show.

• Fix wilderness map background bleeding by reading Duris combined colors in background/foreground order and clearing old backgrounds on foreground-only terrain.
  • Handle background-only map colors, distinguish black from bright black, and reset colors at line and map boundaries.

• Replace the old border artwork with a custom obsidian-and-bronze atlas frame, engraved compass details, and a compact DURIS wordmark.
  • Remove the "New Duris" heading and keep the frame's interior black for readable game output.
• Use a solid black background for the primary MUD text feed and its surrounding panel so incoming text blends with the console.

• Advertise all consumed GMCP packages, including maps, quests and ships.
  • Clear character, combat, ship and map state and cancel pending actions on logout or disconnect.
  • Consume ship navigation and targeting from the server's actual payload fields; keep empty contact lists authoritative.
  • Display nested ship armor, hull, weapons, equipment and cargo data.
  • Read mapper door state from Room.Info.doors.
  • Finish inventory and equipment captures on Telnet prompts, including custom prompts.
  • Show complete server quest descriptions without duplicate Ask/Kill prefixes.
  • Clear combat on the server's end notification, including bleeding targets.
  • Avoid counting buffered text damage again after a GMCP fight ends.

• Load the decorative background using platform-compatible asset paths.
  • Use Mudlet's native command line as the single input and give the reclaimed space to the output console.
  • Display the built package version in the footer.
  • Preserve character state and widgets when hiding and showing the UI.
  • Remove package aliases, triggers, event handlers and delayed actions on uninstall; clean up map download handlers and bound their waits.
  • Keep delayed zone downloads from replacing a newer wilderness map, and report malformed map responses.
  • Clear stale maps when a zone cannot load; refresh using wall time and validate nested map fields.
  • Let room tooltips work through the player marker and keep them inside narrow maps.
  • Show a compact map placeholder until room data arrives.
  • Keep large groups readable in a scrolling panel and retain NPC markers on long names.
  • Recompute group scrolling when members leave so remaining members stay visible.
  • Reset the damage source between fights so text damage works after a GMCP-tracked fight.
  • Accept the server's JSON-null combat target when disengaging without raising a Lua error.
  • Render a numeric zone ID safely when optional room area text is absent.
  • Wrap console text to the available width when resizing.
  • Capture inventory items with capitalized names, bare names and grouped counts; finish empty captures at the prompt.
  • Clear equipment when the server reports nothing worn, remove Duris color codes from identity text, and refresh STATS on room changes using the player score command.

• Use Duris naming in the package metadata, UI messages, documentation, and issue forms.
  • Point zone-map downloads and world-map/wiki links to https://duris.sbs.
  • Rename the packaged background to duris-v1.png and update the UI's asset paths.
  • Point repository and publishing instructions to LuminariMUD/duris-client with origin as the only remote.

New ArjAuto script: the automation and utility side of the "lielz scripts" archive, reworked so nothing is hardcoded to one character. Every automatic behaviour is off until auto <name> on; toggles, variables, the rescue list, bidscores and login commands persist in arjauto.json. Type auto for help.

  • Toggles: autoStand, autoGroup, autoRescue, autoAssist, autoRage, autoWield, autoLoot, autoOre, autoFollow, autoPlay, trapKill, scanReport, eventReport, shipKeys, roller.
  • Variables (vars): target, container, food, weapon, held, door, tank, song, cargo, contra, idscroll, spam, report channel, intervals, roll threshold.
  • Rescue list: rescue add|del|group|list|clear; rescue lag handled with the archive's response lines plus a safety timeout.
  • Combat: kt, bsh, bsht, bash-by-race shortcuts, rbsh/rbsht/bof rebash after the 14 s bash lag, fls flee-stab, bac backstab, uw <item> [target] hold-and-use.
  • Containers and corpses: pcb gcb pab gab lib pi gi grep rrep eat qf rq, lc lcb lic dc nlc slc elc wlc.
  • Movement: door helpers with the dd variable, ep egh emw ewh enl env, sw <dirs>, lall, sfle, fc, of, rm.
  • Group: castall <spell>, vitall, virtueall, weakest.
  • Timers: spam <cmd> with spamon/spamoff, scan timer on|off; both only fire while idle and standing.
  • Ship: oh os fff ffp ffs ffr ffall, orders relative to the locked contact (otf otp ots otr oth otsp), jet disem, farsee le ln lne lnw ls lse lsw lw, ship poll on|off, lout on|off, shipf/shipn, qkcargo, qkreload, Ctrl and Ctrl+Shift hotkeys behind auto shipKeys on.
  • Loot split: split start|roll|free|scores|set|flush with persisted bidscores and multi-die rolls.
  • Identify: id <item> recites your idscroll and compacts the readout to one line.
  • Epic zones: epic report lists zones seen completed this boot.
  • Login commands: login add|list|clear sent when you enter the game.
  • Plane direction notes: dirs eth|astral|air|fire|water|neg.
  • ArjUI's scan summary hands off to ArjAuto for channel reporting; ui help mentions auto.
• Removed the "client-side UI only, no automation" scope statements from the package description, README, and contributor guide. No code changes.

Display helpers ported from the community "lielz scripts" collection (docs/archive/lielz_scripts_04-2024.mpackage). Everything is client-side display; no gameplay automation was carried over. Details in docs/ongoing-projects/lielz-port.md.

  • SHIP tab: contacts sorted by range and colored by side, heading and speed, captain, max speed, lock-on target, and sailing skill gains. Reads GMCP Ship.Info/Ship.Contacts when present and the look contacts text otherwise. First step toward the ship radar noted in the server study.
  • Damage counter in the target panel: per-fight total that resets when a kill or experience share arrives, plus a session report with damage per second (ui damage, ui damage reset, or click the counter). Uses Combat.Update.round or [Damage: N] lines, never both.
  • Experience notices: [+N exp] M to level, about K more like that from GMCP exp/tnl. The TNL bar shows the last gain.
  • Scan formatter: scan lines become [E ] 2 A Drow Elf with distance and direction colored, followed by a per-direction summary.
  • Alert banners for sanctuary, hellfire, stone skin, heroism, rage, and war cry dropping; being disarmed, dropping your weapon, disarm results; being scryed; skill improvements; song finished or failed; frost beacons; and tracks.
  • Group panel: moves percentage per member colored by how spent it is, HP as cur/max -missing, and the most hurt player in the room highlighted.
  • Chat timestamps (hh:mm) on every chat line.
  • Numpad movement keys: 8/2/4/6, 7/9/1/3, - up, + down, 5 look, / scan, 0 flee.
  • Settings: ui set lists six toggles, all on by default and persisted to arjui_settings.json. ui help lists commands.
  • ui debug also reports Ship.Info and Ship.Contacts.

Same package as 1.1, re-released to adopt semantic versioning.

  • Versions are now MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. The build and the release workflow reject anything else.
  • build.py creates the output directory when it is missing.

First tagged release.

  • Aligned ArjUI with the Duris server's GMCP output (Char.Status, Char.Vitals, room, group, and combat fields).
  • Split the package into editable sources under src/ with a stdlib-only build.py assembler.
  • Renamed the build output to duris-client.mpackage.
  • Added GitHub Actions: CI syntax-checks and builds on every push; pushing a v* tag publishes a release with the package attached.
  • Refreshed the README with install steps, an architecture overview, and troubleshooting.
Original Arjinius Client package by Arjinius, as uploaded to the repository.
